title: Traffic-gating experiment framework for pinned models
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable experiment and traffic-gating layer that lets product and platform teams safely run A/B tests and short-lived canary rollouts for model versions that are pinned by customers. The framework should integrate with model onboarding and performance-profile publishing so that new variants surface with metadata (expected latency, cost, quality buckets) and can be automatically gated by policy.

Rationale: Teams are onboarding new model variants more frequently (quantized builds, optimized kernels, sequence-length tuned weights). Many customers pin to a model name but expect Redwood to manage safe rollouts of revisions. Today we lack a first-class experiment layer tied to pins and performance profiles; experiments are ad hoc and risk noisy user experience. This project reduces risk and shipping friction by providing standardized gates, automated metrics checks, and rollback triggers.

Key constraints: must work across hosted and Dedicated; must not require customer changes to existing pin APIs; must respect customer-configured pin semantics (explicit revision pin vs name); must be configurable by teams with RBAC controls.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment API that attaches to existing pin metadata and accepts: variant key, experiment duration, traffic schedule, metric gates, and priority
Can create A/B experiment and routed canary with percent-based traffic splits against a pinned model without changing existing client SDKs (server-side routing only)
Performance-profile publish flow attaches candidate performance metrics to experiment UI automatically
Automated gate evaluation engine that checks live signals every minute and marks experiment state (PASS/WARN/FAIL)
Rollback policy that triggers automatic traffic reversion and alerting within SLO targets when critical gates fail
End-to-end documentation and example for onboarding a new model variant behind a pin
success_metrics: Reduce manual rollbacks for pinned-model revisions by 80% in first quarter after launch
Average time-to-safe-release (canary->general) reduced from 4 days to < 24 hours for model revisions with existing performance profiles
>70% of new model variant onboarding runs use the experiment flow within 3 months
False-positive rollback rate < 2% for major regressions detected by gates
scope: Design and implement server-side experiment orchestration tied to pin metadata, a small web UI in Console for configuring experiments, integration with performance profile registry, metrics evaluation engine, and safety rollback hooks. Initial rollout to hosted and Dedicated only (no full Private on-prem packaging in v1).
non_goals: Client SDK changes, model training/validation tooling, full Private air-gapped installers (these will be follow-ups), automated model retraining based on experiment results.
deliverables: Console experiment composer: create/edit/schedule experiments for pinned models
Gate evaluation service with pluggable metric adapters (latency, cost, eval-pass-rate)
Performance-profile ingestion hook that annotates experiment candidates
Runbook and incident playbook for failed experiments
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Spec and stakeholder alignment (2 weeks) — workshops with runtime, infra, Console, and customer success.
Phase 1: MVP API + gate engine + perf-profile sync (4 weeks) — internal-only experiments and integration tests using synthetic workloads.
Phase 2: Console UI + canary automation (3 weeks) — limited alpha with Platform and two pilot customers.
Phase 3: Public beta and docs (2 weeks) — enable self-serve experiments for hosted customers; monitor.
Phase 4: GA with Dedicated support and RBAC polish (4 weeks) — production SLA and support docs.
Traffic schedule defaults: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with configurable durations (default 30m/1h/2h/6h/24h).
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary gates: latency P95 increase > 25% over baseline, error-rate increase > 2x baseline, token-cost delta > 15% vs pinned baseline, eval-pass-rate drop > 3 percentage points on curated prompt set. Secondary signals: tail-latency P99, memory OOMs, KV-cache hit-rate degradation. Alerts: Pager for P0 gate failures, Slack channel for WARN states, automated rollback for FAIL states. All experiments emit structured events to telemetry with experiment_id, variant, step, and gate-status.
